title: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP): Clinical Mastery
summary: ROP is a proliferative vitreoretinopathy affecting the developing retinal vasculature of preterm infants. Understanding the International Classification of ROP (ICROP3) is vital for timely screening and preventing irreversible blindness through laser or anti-VEGF therapy.

sections.title: Clinical Red Flags
content: Plus Disease: Venous dilation and arteriolar tortuosity in at least two quadrants.
Pre-plus: Vascular abnormality insufficient for plus disease but abnormal.
Aggressive ROP (A-ROP): Rapidly progressive, posterior, often flat, without classic stages.
Failure to recognize 'Notch' in vascular pattern indicating skip areas.

sections.title: Screening Guidelines (AAP/AAO)
content: Step 1: First exam at 31 weeks CA or 4 weeks postnatal (whichever is later).
Step 2: Infants > 1500g or > 30 weeks GA at discretion of neonatologist.
Step 3: Follow-up weekly or bi-weekly based on retinal maturity and stage.
Step 4: Stop at vascularization to Zone III (approx 45 weeks CA).

content.explanation: P: Posterior pole involvement, L: Lacerated/dilated vessels, U: U-turn vessels, S: Stasis/Tortuosity.

rows: Autosomal dominant, older children, family history
Unilateral, microphthalmos, stalk to optic nerve

sections.title: Treatment Modalities
content: Laser Photocoagulation: Peripheral retinal ablation (Gold standard).
Anti-VEGF (Bevacizumab): Inject 0.625mg into vitreous cavity; effective for Zone I disease.
Surgical Vitrectomy: Indicated for Stage 4B and 5 RD; lensectomy often required.
Scleral Buckling: Indicated for detached retinas with open funnel in selected cases.

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
content: CRYO-ROP (1988): Established cryotherapy as effective treatment.
ETROP (2003): Defined 'Type 1 ROP' requiring immediate intervention.
BEAT-ROP (2011): Demonstrated efficacy of intravitreal Bevacizumab, especially in Zone I.
RAINBOW Study: Confirmed efficacy of Ranibizumab vs Laser.
